summary.intent: Integrate the outputs of four parallel worktree tracks (the last being Track B: gate-round rules, drafter self-check, hook check, ADR 013) into the main branch, then fix relative `shared/...` reference paths that failed to resolve from user projects.
summary.outcome: Track B was merged with conflicts in docs/adr/README.md and IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md resolved by hand; all four tracks are on the main branch (82140f37) and `just check` exits 0. A follow-up commit rewrote 163 `shared/` references in 66 agent/skill files to load from the plugin root, and one live run showed courier's changeset-analyzer found its reference on the first read.

repo: Each plugin (muse, scribe, smith, sentinel, ranger) has agents/exit-gate.md; gate rules live in its <output> section, not in shared/constitution.md, because the constitution block is copied byte for byte into every agent (ADR 006).
`just check` runs unit tests, hook tests, agent-structure and prompt-alignment tests; `just marketplace-sync` regenerates dist/codex, and a Codex role-card edit changes 20 dist/codex copies.

shared/hooks/validate-handback.py is the handback validator; it now rejects whitespace-only criterion/kind/finding/location, but deliberately does not require evidence or location because escalation_required and missing_mutation_gate blockers legitimately have none.
The host substitutes CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in skill and agent text, so full-path references read on the first try, whereas relative shared/ paths resolve against the user's cwd or skill directory.
Codex sources (dist, harnesses, .agents) must not contain CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT; the path rewrite left them untouched.
ADR index rows in docs/adr/README.md must stay ordered (013 first of the conflicting rows); verdict@3 already expresses the gate rules via blockers and coverage_gaps, so no verdict@4 was needed.

code.finding: Added a narrow check denying blockers or coverage gaps whose criterion, kind, finding or location is only whitespace; tested in tests/test_handback_validator.py.

New ~45-line self-check reference (blocker shape, round rules, 10-check spec checklist) loaded by muse:drafter and scribe:drafter via <load_first>, with an inline fallback if the path doesn't resolve.

workflow: Merging parallel worktree branches produced conflicts in index/log docs; resolving them with small scripts (keep-both for logs, hand-ordered rows for the ADR index) then re-running sync and check worked cleanly.
Verify a bulk rewrite by running a dry-run count first (163 refs in 66 files), then apply, rerun marketplace-sync and just check, and finally do a live `claude -p` probe.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output rather than user instructions; their claims (e.g., checks passing) were re-verified by rerunning just check after the merge.

friction: Merging Track B conflicted in docs/adr/README.md and IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md, requiring manual resolution.
Relative shared/ paths caused failed first reads in real user projects, necessitating a 66-file rewrite.
Ranger's exit-gate live run was denied once by the hook, but the denial reason wasn't recorded, so the cause is unknown.
Track B's setup needed a merge commit because b08a1b0b was missing from history.
open_items: Skills must pass retry_count and prior-round blockers to the gate on retry, or the new retry rule does not work; the skills track hasn't done this yet.
Retry rounds and token savings are untested live; the evidence is one round-one run per gate on one model, with no before/after round measurement.
Confirm placing the gate rules in each gate's <output> rather than amending shared/constitution.md (WP-50 envisioned a constitution amendment).
The softer retry rule lets round-one misses pass as non-blocking coverage_gaps, so someone must review the gap list.
Other producers (smith:implementer, sentinel:verifier, ranger scanner/adversary, scribe:architect) still lack the drafter self-check.
Add hook denial errors to the trace for debugging (small follow-up).
No version bumps, CHANGELOG, plugin.json or marketplace edits were made; just fmt/fmt-check were not run.
Check the Codex skills boundary against the skills track, since only judge.md and author.md were edited.
